rows: Advance a date by N trading sessions, skipping non-sessions (exchange 'XNYS')

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Advance a date by **N trading sessions**, skipping the exchange's non-session days. The `exchange` argument is optional and defaults to `'XNYS'` (NYSE); pass a MIC code (e.g. `'XLON'`) for another market. `N` may be negative to step backwards; the result is always a trading session. Returns `DATE` per row (`NULL` inputs -> `NULL`); `NULL` if outside the calendar's coverage window. List valid codes with `tcal.exchanges`.

rows: Per-session open/close/early-close schedule for a date range

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Return the **per-session trading schedule over an inclusive `[start, end]` date range**: one row per session with its `session` date, UTC `market_open` and `market_close` instants, and an `is_early_close` flag. Takes `start` and `end` positionally plus an optional named `exchange` (default `'XNYS'`, NYSE). This is the set-returning companion to the scalar `market_open` / `market_close` / `is_early_close` functions -- use it to materialize a market-hours table for a period (note half-days like the day after Thanksgiving). Sessions outside the coverage window are omitted. See `tcal.exchanges` for MIC codes.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## trading_schedule(start, end, exchange := ...)

Per-session **open / close / early-close schedule** over `[start, end]`.

One row per session: `session`, UTC `market_open`/`market_close`, `is_early_close`. `exchange` defaults to `'XNYS'`. Materializes a market-hours table (half-days flagged). See `tcal.exchanges`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Half-days in the NYSE Thanksgiving-week schedule, with their early close time.", "sql": "SELECT session, market_close FROM tcal.main.trading_schedule(DATE '2026-11-25', DATE '2026-11-30') WHERE is_early_close"}, {"description": "Every NYSE early-close half-day in 2026 with its early close time (UTC) and when the market next opens -- how long positions sit over the holiday break.", "sql": "SELECT sc.session, sc.market_close, tcal.main.next_trading_day(sc.session) AS next_session, tcal.main.market_open(tcal.main.next_trading_day(sc.session)) AS next_open FROM tcal.main.trading_schedule(DATE '2026-01-01', DATE '2026-12-31') AS sc WHERE sc.is_early_close ORDER BY sc.session"}, {"description": "Minutes of overlap between NYSE and London trading hours on sessions both trade in March-April 2026: usually 2 hours, widening to 3 hours for the weeks when the US has moved to daylight saving time and the UK has not.", "sql": "SELECT date_diff('minute', greatest(ny.market_open, ln.market_open), least(ny.market_close, ln.market_close)) AS overlap_minutes, count(*) AS n_sessions, min(ny.session) AS first_session FROM tcal.main.trading_schedule(DATE '2026-03-01', DATE '2026-04-30') AS ny JOIN tcal.main.trading_schedule(DATE '2026-03-01', DATE '2026-04-30', exchange := 'XLON') AS ln USING (session) GROUP BY overlap_minutes ORDER BY first_session"}]
rows.vgi.keywords: ["trading schedule", "market hours", "open close times", "session schedule", "early close", "half day", "trading hours table", "nyse schedule"]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "session", "type": "DATE", "description": "Trading session date."}, {"name": "market_open", "type": "TIMESTAMPTZ", "description": "UTC market-open instant."}, {"name": "market_close", "type": "TIMESTAMPTZ", "description": "UTC market-close instant."}, {"name": "is_early_close", "type": "BOOLEAN", "description": "True if the session closes early."}]
rows.vgi.title: Trading Schedule For Range

rows: Every trading session in an inclusive [start, end] range

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Enumerate **every trading session in an inclusive `[start, end]` date range**, one per row -- the days the market is open, excluding weekends and exchange holidays. Takes `start` and `end` positionally plus an optional named `exchange` (default `'XNYS'`, NYSE). Both bounds are inclusive. Use it to expand a range into a session series you can join against, count, or window over. Dates outside the `exchange-calendars` coverage window simply do not appear. For other markets pass `exchange`; see `tcal.exchanges` for MIC codes.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
## trading_sessions(start, end, exchange := ...)

Every **trading session in the inclusive `[start, end]` range**, one per row.

Open days only (no weekends/holidays); `exchange` defaults to `'XNYS'`. Expand a range into a session series for joins/counts. See `tcal.exchanges`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Count the NYSE trading sessions in January 2026.", "sql": "SELECT count(*) AS n_sessions FROM tcal.main.trading_sessions(DATE '2026-01-01', DATE '2026-01-31')"}, {"description": "The last London Stock Exchange sessions of January 2026 (26th onward).", "sql": "SELECT session FROM tcal.main.trading_sessions(DATE '2026-01-01', DATE '2026-01-31', exchange := 'XLON') WHERE session >= DATE '2026-01-26'"}, {"description": "NYSE sessions in 2026 on which the London Stock Exchange is closed (UK bank holidays such as Easter Monday and the Boxing Day substitute) -- days a US/UK pairs desk trades only one leg.", "sql": "SELECT s.session FROM tcal.main.trading_sessions(DATE '2026-01-01', DATE '2026-12-31') AS s WHERE NOT tcal.main.is_trading_day(s.session, 'XLON') ORDER BY s.session"}, {"description": "T+1 settlement date for a trade on each NYSE session of Thanksgiving week 2026 -- the Wednesday trade settles on Friday because the Thanksgiving holiday is skipped.", "sql": "SELECT s.session AS trade_date, tcal.main.add_trading_days(s.session, 1) AS settles_t1 FROM tcal.main.trading_sessions(DATE '2026-11-23', DATE '2026-11-30') AS s ORDER BY s.session"}]
rows.vgi.keywords: ["trading sessions", "list sessions", "market days", "open days", "session series", "trading calendar", "nyse sessions", "date range"]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "session", "type": "DATE", "description": "A trading session date in the range."}]
